ops.title: daemonSocketMismatch broke ccp add: which side was stale
ops.body:
`ccp add` failed deterministically with `daemonkit: business session: context deadline exceeded` plus a `retire reserved FuseKit tenant: ... catalog: not found` rollback tail. Not a timeout to raise — the FuseKit broker child could not start at all.

**Chain.** fusekit `holder/runtime.go:145` derives `r.socket = dkpaths.Socket(agent.Label)`; `holder/runtime.go:648` threads it into the broker child argv `--fusekit-daemon-socket`. The signed app compares it against its own constant at `Sources/FuseKit/Broker.swift:106` and throws `daemonSocketMismatch` (visible in `~/.cc-pool/fusekit/broker.log`). Broker never starts → `fusekit.sock` never bound → provisioning blocks → the client deadline, which rides the wire into the daemon-side handler, expires there → rollback retires a tenant that was never created.

**The trap: which side is stale.** Both fusekit's own Go tests (`holder/broker_process_test.go:83,566`, passing `plan.Paths().Socket`) and cc-pool's Swift constant expect `<runtimeDir>/fusekit.sock`. That agreement looks like independent corroboration and is not — they are one pre-migration layout reflected twice, and both are stale.

**Proof the Go side is live.** `RuntimePaths.Socket` has exactly three readers in all of fusekit: a length check (`holder/plan.go:424`), a digest field (`holder/plan.go:637`), and the argv line. **Nothing binds or listens on it.** Meanwhile `lsof` shows CCPoolStatus binding `~/com.yasyf.cc-pool.status.fusekit/daemon.sock` — i.e. `r.socket`. A live experiment dialing the Swift constant's path returned `connect errno 2` (ENOENT).

So "fix the Go launcher to match the tests and the Swift config" is the wrong fix: it makes the guard pass and then the broker fails to connect — a quieter failure than the original.

**Introduced by** fusekit `b313adf` (2026-08-03, "migrate to daemonkit v0.21.3"), which added the `socket` parameter to `newBrokerProcessOwner`, wired production to `r.socket`, and updated the tests to `plan.Paths().Socket` — which is why CI stayed green over a broken binary.

**Not fixed upstream.** cc-pool `2a62759` ("adapt the broker configuration to FuseKit v1.16") deliberately carried `holderSocketPath` forward when it dropped `expectedRuntimeBuild`/`noProgressTimeout`; the constant is still `.cc-pool/fusekit/fusekit.sock` at origin/main.

Related: see the note on the broker↔daemon peer-verification gap — the mismatch is the availability symptom; the missing listener check is the security defect underneath.
